claims.statement: Game data from DofusDB is read-only in the panel and refreshed by a script, and Torre picks it through relationship fields.

The DofusDB client pages collections in pages of 50 until the reported total or an empty page, optionally restricting each row to selected fields with $select[] parameters, and fetches records by ID deduplicated in chunks of 40 using id[$in][] filters.

The DofusDB client waits 50 ms between requests, sends the User-Agent ta-web/datos-del-juego, gives each request a 30-second timeout, and accepts injected fetch, sleep, log and random so tests never reach the network.

fetchQuestData loads every DofusDB quest, fetches by ID only the NPCs and map positions referenced by the quests' start positions and the monsters named in their computed needs, and downloads the whole item catalog with fetchAll, selecting only id, name, level, typeId, iconId and type.

mapQuest names a quest in Spanish, falling back to French and then to 'Misión <id>', keeps the raw startCriterion, and builds start positions with NPC names and map coordinates, leaving nulls when a lookup is missing instead of failing.

Quest prerequisites are only the Qf=<id> terms joined by & in startCriterion; a level containing | is treated as alternatives and contributes none, other terms such as Qa= are ignored, and the result is deduplicated and excludes the quest itself.

DofusDB's need.quests is not used for prerequisites because it lists every quest mentioned in the criterion: quest 275 lists 272, 273 and 274 for (Qf=272|Qf=273|Qf=274) and gets no prerequisites, and quest 879 lists 871 and 878 for Qf=871&Qa=878 and gets only 871.

refreshQuests writes quests through the local API with overrideAccess true in two passes: first creating or updating quest fields by dofusId only when they differ, then linking prerequisites by Payload ID and skipping and counting missing ones.

A refresh with unchanged data writes nothing, refreshedAt is set only on rows created or changed in that run, nothing is ever deleted, and the function returns created, updated and unchanged counts for quests, items and monsters plus missing prerequisite, item and monster counts.

pnpm data:quests runs scripts/refresh-quests.ts with payload run; the script starts Payload with getPayload, writes to the DATABASE_URL database or the pnpm db:dev one when it is empty, prints counts, and exits with code 1 on failure because payload run otherwise exits 0.
A full refresh downloads about 2,000 quests, about 1,000 monsters and the whole item catalog of about 21,500 items from DofusDB, and a rerun changes only what DofusDB changed without deleting rows.
Payload schema push runs only under next dev, so other processes rely on applied migrations.
Agent access rules grant full access to dev and read access to prod; prod writes, including database changes, go through release.yml or need Daniel's explicit yes for that one action.
Game data from DofusDB is refreshed on demand after an Ankama patch.
Nothing loads from DofusDB or Ankama at runtime; item and monster icons are stored only as DofusDB image IDs.

mapItem and mapMonster name rows in Spanish with a French fallback and then 'Objeto <id>' or 'Monstruo <id>', keep an item's level, typeId and iconId plus its superTypeId from type.superTypeId, and store a monster's gfxId as iconId.

questRewards computes rewards for a level-200 character from the last rewards entry of each step, using fixe(L) = L(100+2L)^2/20 x duration x experienceRatio, XP = fixe(200) when the optimal level is at least 200 and otherwise 0.3 fixe(opt) + 0.7 fixe(min(200, 1.5 opt)), and kamas = (opt^2 + 20 opt - 20) x kamasRatio x duration.
Reward XP and kamas are floored per step before summing, so quest 241 yields 5,679,336 XP rather than the 5,679,337 a single final floor would give.
Quest 1977 yields 24,316 XP and 552 kamas, matching Torre's guide and dofusdb.fr.
Reward items are summed by item across steps, and emote, spell, title and job reward IDs are collected without duplicates as plain DofusDB IDs.

questNeeds takes delivered items from BringItemToNpc objectives, monsters from FightMonster, MultiFightMonster, FightMonstersOnMap and BringSoulToNpc objectives, sets walksMaps for DiscoverMap and DiscoverSubArea objectives, and ignores FreeForm, GoToNpc, CraftItem and other objectives.

Because DofusDB's need.items summary already includes delivered items, questNeeds keeps the larger of the need.items and delivered quantities instead of their sum, so quest 245 needs 2 of item 8993, not 3.

A quest guide's Necesitarás item list is copied from the linked quest's computed needs.items without quest items of supertype 14, while Torre's editorial Necesitarás text stays in the guide's summary.needs.notes, which the fill never touches.

Before the quests, refreshQuests creates or updates items and then monsters by dofusId only when they change, and resolves reward and need references to their Payload IDs, dropping and counting references with no stored row.

mapWithConcurrency returns results in input order, runs at most limit calls at once, starts nothing new after the first error and rejects with that error once running calls settle, and throws a RangeError for a limit that is not an integer of at least 1.

Within each step (items, monsters, the quests' first pass and the prerequisites pass) refreshQuests writes rows concurrently with mapWithConcurrency, keeping the steps in the same order, with options.concurrency defaulting to DEFAULT_WRITE_CONCURRENCY, which is 8.
refreshQuests sums its created, updated, unchanged and missing counts from the result each write returns rather than from shared counters.
The refresh source notes that writing rows one at a time took about half an hour against Neon because each write is several round trips to the database.
writeConcurrencyFromEnv returns 8 when DOFUSDB_WRITE_CONCURRENCY is empty or unset and throws on any value that is not an integer of at least 1.
Each concurrent write holds one Postgres pool connection; the pool sets no explicit max, so pg's default of 10 applies, and .env.example advises not going above 9.
scripts/refresh-quests.ts reads DOFUSDB_WRITE_CONCURRENCY before starting Payload, prints how many writes run at once and prints the write phase time.
An integration test runs the refresh over both fixtures with concurrency 1 and then with concurrency 8 and expects equal counts and equal stored data, comparing relationships by DofusDB ID.
The DofusDB client retries network errors and HTTP 429, 502, 503 and 504 up to 4 times, waiting 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 seconds each plus up to 25% random jitter, and does not retry any other non-2xx status.
On a 429 the client waits for the Retry-After header, read as seconds or an HTTP date and capped at 60 seconds, falling back to the computed backoff when the header is missing or unreadable.

When retries run out or a status is not retryable, the client throws a Spanish error naming the URL and the number of attempts, keeping the network error as its cause, and its optional log callback receives one line per retry.
pnpm data:quests passes console.log to the DofusDB client so each retry prints a line.
While writing items or monsters, refreshCatalog logs progress every 2,000 saved rows because the item catalog exceeds 20,000 rows.

A quest guide's summary is copied from the linked quest's prerequisites and PL> level, rewards and first start position, and later refreshes do not change existing guides because only empty guide fields are filled.

requiredTerms in src/lib/dofusdb/criterion.ts returns the criterion terms joined by & at the top level or inside &-only brackets, in order, returns nothing for a level containing |, and returns an empty list for a missing or empty criterion; mapQuest prerequisites and the guide's requiredLevel both use it.
